Headline: **On the RLVR-trained distribution, RLVR leaves the linear context→answer map exactly as far from base-reconstructible as DPO does — the registered contrast C = Δ_RLVR − Δ_DPO is −0.00003 with a 1000-draw paired-bootstrap 95% CI of [−0.00237, +0.00223] (gsm8k_train5k chat, layer 30, recalibrated scale). The reparameterization gap itself is stage-UNIFORM: +0.139 (SFT), +0.133 (DPO), +0.133 (RLVR) — whatever map change post-training makes is complete at the SFT stage, and RLVR adds nothing detectable at ±0.002 precision.** Registered lattice verdict: `inconclusive` (C's CI includes 0 — neither CI-clear positive nor wholly below 0); `h_elicit_supported: false`; `h_generic_flagged: false`. ### What was measured (sign convention — read this first)

Per stage k and eval set, the reparameterization gap is **Δ_k = R²_within(k) − R²_comp(k)**: the stage's own held-out 5-fold GCV-ridge map (context activation → mean answer activation, on the stage's own on-policy text) minus the composition `A_ans ∘ M_base ∘ A_ctx_rev` evaluated on the same rows and folds (base map in base coordinates, linearly re-coordinatized both sides). Under plan v9 route 1, BOTH arms receive an independent held-out cross-fitted per-dim affine recalibration (the primary scale); raw pooled R² is the companion, reported separately and never averaged. Positive Δ = the stage map carries linear structure the reparameterized base map cannot express (the "teaching" direction). Negative Δ = the composition out-predicts the stage's own directly-fit map — which a well-estimated within arm can never do (the composition is itself a linear map from the same inputs), so a large negative gap is an ESTIMATOR shortfall of the within arm, not a science result. Both signs occur here (below), so gap MAGNITUDES are read per-corpus with their construct caveats; only the stage CONTRAST C (a within-corpus difference of two gaps sharing the same estimator regime) carries the headline.

### Result 1 — the registered headline: no RLVR-specific map change (C ≈ 0 at ±0.002)

### Result 2 — the gap construct behaves on GSM8K-train, fails on LMSYS; the +0.13 gap is a SFT-stage effect with a named confound

Per-pair L30 values (`ladder_alignment/pair_base__*`): on gsm8k_train5k the fits are healthy — λ audit 0/160 at the grid edge, raw ≈ recal (e.g. RLVR within raw +0.4559 vs recal +0.4553), within (0.455–0.464) > composition (0.322–0.329) for every post-trained stage; on lmsys the post-trained within arms are the G1-saga cells — raw within −0.38 to −0.51, recovered to +0.25–0.29 by recalibration, λ audit 37–143/160 at the low edge — and the composition OUT-predicts them (0.41–0.43 recal), giving the −0.13 to −0.16 "impossible-sign" gaps. So the lmsys gap magnitudes are estimator-limited (the composition's 0.43 also shows the linear map on lmsys is genuinely ≥0.43 strong — the E1-adopted within read understates it); the gsm8k_train magnitudes are the trustworthy ones.

On the trustworthy set the interpretation lattice reads: the elicitation criterion fails (Δ ≈ +0.13 ≫ the 0.02 band at every post-trained stage) — the #825 Qwen result (gap 0.0003) does NOT extend as-is to this family/distribution. But the failure is NOT RLVR-shaped: it appears in full at SFT. One named confound before reading "+0.13 = SFT teaches the map": the composition routes through the BASE model's own map M_base, and the Llama base's map on GSM8K is weak (cell S_r 0.177 at full n, below the 0.2012 usable-strength bar; raw rep-swap b2i +0.438 ≈ within +0.456 shows base ACTIVATIONS carry nearly all the predictive information — the bottleneck is the base model's own answer policy/map on math text, where its generations run 8.6% truncated). "Post-training changed the answer distribution the base map was fit on" and "post-training taught new map structure" are not separable in this design; on Qwen the base anchor was strong (0.588) so #825 never faced this. ### Result 3 — the GSM8K-test cell is degenerate by construction (investigated first, as directed)

All four pairs on gsm8k_test1319_chat read within == composition to ~1e-5 (e.g. base→RLVR L30: within_recal +0.245039 vs comp_recal +0.245045; identical pattern at L16/21/22 and for SFT/DPO/RLVR-long). Root cause established, not a data bug: with n=1,293 kept rows (n_train ≈ 1,034 per fold) ≪ d=4,096, GCV selects the λ grid FLOOR (0.01) for **160/160** (layer, fold) fits in every gsm8k_test cell (`cells_*_gsm8k_test1319.json` λ audits), and the alignment maps use the same grid (`issue825_map_alignment.LAMBDAS`). In that near-interpolation regime every component map reproduces its training targets almost exactly, so the composition collapses algebraically to the SAME kernel smoother as the direct within fit — for a test row x, both predictions are the identical weighted combination of training-row targets (the within map and A_ctx_rev share the same X_k Gram matrix and the same λ; M_base and A_ans then act as near-exact interpolators on the training rows) — leaving a residue of order λ (~1e-5). The Δ_k read on this eval set is therefore vacuous FOR ANY model pair; the within-stage recal values themselves are fine (0.246–0.271 at L30, above bar). Supporting parity: the matched-n (1,319-row) refits of gsm8k_TRAIN also land at 160/160 λ-floor and read ≈ the test cell (e.g. RLVR matched-train S_r 0.338 vs test 0.330) — the train-vs-test difference at full n is an n-regime artifact, not contamination evidence.

Planned-vs-actual coverage caveat: the plan's decontaminated-generalization companion — one of the two Bonferroni-2 secondary family members — is thereby uninformative for the gap/contrast DV. The "trained-prompt memorization vs domain-level map change" separation the test split was registered to provide is NOT available from this run; every gap/contrast figure labels the cell degenerate rather than plotting it as a real zero.

### What was measured (sign convention — read this first)

Per stage k and eval set, the reparameterization gap is **Δ_k = R²_within(k) − R²_comp(k)**: the stage's own held-out 5-fold GCV-ridge map (context activation → mean answer activation, on the stage's own on-policy text) minus the composition `A_ans ∘ M_base ∘ A_ctx_rev` evaluated on the same rows and folds (base map in base coordinates, linearly re-coordinatized both sides). Under plan v9 route 1, BOTH arms receive an independent held-out cross-fitted per-dim affine recalibration (the primary scale); raw pooled R² is the companion, reported separately and never averaged. Positive Δ = the stage map carries linear structure the reparameterized base map cannot express (the "teaching" direction). Negative Δ = the composition out-predicts the stage's own directly-fit map — which a well-estimated within arm can never do (the composition is itself a linear map from the same inputs), so a large negative gap is an ESTIMATOR shortfall of the within arm, not a science result. Both signs occur here (below), so gap MAGNITUDES are read per-corpus with their construct caveats; only the stage CONTRAST C (a within-corpus difference of two gaps) carries the headline — and the shared-estimator-regime premise behind reading C as estimator-cancelling holds ON THE HEADLINE SET ONLY (every post-trained gsm8k_train λ selection interior, 0/160 at either grid edge). On lmsys it does NOT hold: the per-stage λ-floor fractions differ (SFT 41, DPO 143, RLVR 110 of 160 on chat), so a nonzero lmsys C could be produced by the estimator regime alone — one reason the lmsys C reads stay secondary (Result 1).

### Result 3 — the GSM8K-test cell is degenerate by construction (investigated first, as directed)

All four pairs on gsm8k_test1319_chat read within == composition to ~1e-5 (e.g. base→RLVR L30: within_recal +0.245039 vs comp_recal +0.245045; identical pattern at L16/21/22 and for SFT/DPO/RLVR-long). Root cause established, not a data bug: with n=1,293 kept rows (n_train ≈ 1,034 per fold) ≪ d=4,096, GCV selects the λ grid FLOOR (0.01) for **160/160** (layer, fold) fits in every gsm8k_test cell (`cells_*_gsm8k_test1319.json` λ audits), and the alignment maps use the same grid (`issue825_map_alignment.LAMBDAS`). In that near-interpolation regime every component map reproduces its training targets almost exactly, so the composition collapses algebraically to the SAME kernel smoother as the direct within fit — for a test row x, both predictions are the identical weighted combination of training-row targets (the within map and A_ctx_rev share the same X_k Gram matrix and the same λ; M_base and A_ans then act as near-exact interpolators on the training rows) — leaving a residue of order λ (~1e-5). The Δ_k read on this eval set is therefore vacuous FOR ANY model pair; the within-stage recal values themselves are fine (0.246–0.271 at L30, above bar). Supporting parity: the matched-n (1,319-row) refits of gsm8k_TRAIN also land at 160/160 λ-floor and read ≈ the test cell (e.g. RLVR matched-train S_r 0.338 vs test 0.330) — the train-vs-test difference at full n is an n-regime artifact, not contamination evidence. (The λ grid saturates at BOTH edges across this design: small-n cells at the floor — this result — and base-model cells at the ceiling — Result 2; the updated λ-edge figure shows both.)

# The Llama Tülu ladder's DPO→RLVR step needs at most a rotation of the linear context→answer map, and on six of eight corpora needs no coordinate change at all (HIGH confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

**Methodology:** [docs/methodology/issue_1336.md](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/blob/2249cf495d8c2d355b2f37f7b84eb7bf396f005d/docs/methodology/issue_1336.md) · [gist mirror](https://gist.github.com/superkaiba/5575c7b1da67014bf781a56e30ca6b88) *(rounds 1–2; the round-3 metric-ladder recipe is added inline under Methodology below and will be re-exported by the orchestrator on promotion.)*

## Takeaways

- **Round-3 headline (this round):** across 7 stage-pairs × 8 corpora (46,000 real-user + 30,600 verifiable-mix prompts, layer 30), the DPO map applied AS-IS to RLVR contexts explains the RLVR within-stage held-out R² on six of eight corpora within a 0.021-wide elicitation band around zero; the other two (MATH, IF-constraints — both in the RLVR training mix) close at a fitted rotation. No linear reparameterization of contexts or answers is required at the RLVR step.
- **The one-shot SFT jump replicates:** the base map (with any linear reparameterization allowed) never reconstructs a post-trained stage's map — every base→⟨SFT, DPO, RLVR, longer RLVR⟩ tier-8 gap is +0.14 to +0.23 across every one of the 8 corpora, orders of magnitude above the band. Post-training installs the map at SFT, and every later step is a coordinate change or nothing.
- **RLVR is closer to DPO than DPO is to SFT:** on the six RLVR-mix or DPO-mix corpora (GSM8K, MATH, IF, UF, LMSYS × 2 renders), DPO→RLVR needs at most a rotation (tier ≤ 5) on 7/8 corpora, while SFT→DPO needs an answer-side or full linear reparameterization (tier 7–8) on 5/8 corpora and "none suffices" on 3/8.
- **Longer-RLVR (Tülu-3.1) is comparable to RLVR:** DPO→longer-RLVR closes at rotation or below on 4/8 corpora and "none" on 2/8, with two intermediate corpora (MATH, GSM8K train) closing at t5–t8; no dose increase past the RLVR step.
- **Scope: one released ladder** (Llama-3.1-8B Tülu-3), a single manipulated variable (post-training stage), fits on independently held-out folds with full paired-bootstrap CIs (1,000 draws) and layer 30 the plan-registered headline. The two RLVR-trained corpora where DPO→RLVR does not fold to a rotation (MATH, IF-constraints) are the only positive evidence for RLVR-specific map change; both have delta_tier8 ≤ +0.025 and are the corpora RLVR actually trained on.

## Goal

- **This experiment in context:** The parent experiment [#825](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/825) found, on Qwen2.5-7B, that post-training does not create the linear context→answer map: the pretrained model already carries it at 87% of instruct strength, and the instruct map is reconstructible from the base map by a general linear change of coordinates to within 0.0003 R² (the map construct comes from [#779](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/779)). Qwen2.5 predates RLVR, so that elicitation-not-teaching read was confined to SFT/DPO-era post-training. Round 1 extended the read to an RL-with-verifiable-rewards stage using the only released ladder with separately published SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints (Llama-3.1-8B Tülu-3) at 5,000-prompt scope, finding a precise headline null. Round 3 (this round) extends the corpus scope to the full GSM8K train (7,473), a 15,000-kept LMSYS slice, and four stage-matched corpora (MATH 7,500; IF-constraints 11,000; UltraFeedback 11,000; Tülu-3 SFT-mix 11,000), and replaces the single reparameterization gap with the 9-tier metric ladder — direct transfer → context/answer/bias offsets → global scaling → rotation → linear reparameterization of contexts / answers / both — so "elicitation" is resolved into *which* correction class suffices per stage-pair × corpus.
- **Broader narrative:** This serves the contextual-vs-base identity question (`docs/open_questions.md`, identity-contextual-vs-base anchor): does post-training teach new context→answer structure, or re-expose structure the pretrained model already has? RLVR on verifiable rewards is the strongest published candidate for genuine teaching, so a tight null across the DPO→RLVR pair — plus the resolution that the SFT→DPO step needs a strictly higher tier than the DPO→RLVR step — is the most informative single read available for the elicitation-not-teaching account.

## Methodology

**Design:** Five released checkpoints of one ladder — `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B` (base), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-DPO`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B` (post-RLVR), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3.1-8B` (longer-RLVR) — crossed in round 3 with eight prompt corpora and one render format per corpus, giving 40 generation cells and 56 stage-pair × corpus × layer-30 metric-ladder pair files (7 stage-pairs × 8 corpora). The post-training stage is the single manipulated variable; corpora, renders, sampling, and the fit recipe are held fixed. Round 3 corpora (revision-pinned): `chat` render on GSM8K test (1,319), GSM8K train full (7,473), MATH (7,500 from the RLVR mix), IF-constraints (11,000 sampled from the RLVR mix's ifeval component), UltraFeedback prompts (11,000 from the Tülu-3 8B preference mixture), Tülu-3 SFT-mix (11,000, stratified 3,667/3,667/3,666 across wildchat/flan/evol-codealpaca), and LMSYS-Chat-1M (23,000 sampled to yield ~15,000 kept); `naturalistic` render on LMSYS only. Rounds 1–2 (5,000 LMSYS × 2 renders + 5,000 GSM8K train + 1,319 GSM8K test) are superseded by the fatter round-3 corpora except the GSM8K test cell, which is retained as the decontaminated companion. Per the standing both-mappings rule, the context-based mapping ran on every corpus × format; the prefix-based mapping (`xprefix`) ran on `naturalistic_lmsys23k` only — the chat-template prefix slot is row-constant by construction (measured max pairwise cosine distance up to 1.5e-4), so its map is degenerate at every stage. The naturalistic prefix mapping ran and reads R² 0.001–0.005 across all five stages (base 0.005; SFT/DPO/RLVR/longer-RLVR all 0.001) — floor-limited, invariant across stages, carried as an uncovered signal cell (a scope caveat, not a null).

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** Round 3 spent 194.37 GPU-h against a budgeted 98 GPU-h (2.0× over budget; deviation from plan §11, recorded here; the fit + metric-ladder phase's per-cell wall was under-estimated at plan time — the pilot batteries measured 541s/corpus vs the planned 1.4 h/corpus, but the mass of stage-corpus cells at 15–17k rows in generation + capture drove the wall).

**Evaluation:** Per (stage-pair p, corpus s, layer L=30) the reparameterization ladder produces held-out R² of the source map applied to target contexts at every tier t ∈ {0..8}, on the same rows and folds as the target's within-stage map. Tiers, per `docs/mapping_similarity_metrics.md`: t0 direct transfer (ŷ = W_s x + b_s applied unchanged), t1 context offset (ŷ = W_s (x − Δx) + b_s, Δx from cloud means only), t2 answer offset (Δy on the output side), t3 bias offset (refit b* only), t4 global scaling (α W_s x + b*), t5 mapping rotation (R W_s x + b*, orthogonal Procrustes on directions), t6 linear reparameterization of contexts (source map through A: target→source context linear map), t7 linear reparameterization of answers (B: target→source answer linear map), t8 both (A ∘ W_s ∘ B). All offsets fit on clouds alone (never on paired context→answer rows). The gap per tier is Δ_t = within-stage R² − tier-t R². The registered sufficient-tier statistic is sufficient_tier(p, s) = min{t ∈ 0..8 : Δ_t ≤ 0.021 · ex_v2 = 0.0207} at the paired prompt-level bootstrap point estimate; "none ≤ 8" is a reportable value meaning no tier's linear reparameterization closes the within-vs-transfer gap within the band. Primary scale is raw pooled R² (round 3's fatter fold-train regime makes the recalibration rescue used in rounds 1–2 unnecessary — G0v2/G1v2 both PASS at raw); the held-out cross-fitted per-dim affine recalibration companion is always computed. The stage-of-record contrast C_v2 = Δ_tier8(RLVR, gsm8k_train_full, chat) − Δ_tier8(DPO, gsm8k_train_full, chat) on the RLVR training distribution: point −0.0031 with a bootstrap 95% CI running from −0.0039 to −0.0024 on the raw scale (a signed negative CI — reparameterized-DPO reconstructs RLVR SLIGHTLY better than reparameterized-base reconstructs DPO on that corpus; magnitude smaller than the elicit band by a factor of five). Registered decision constants (round-3 revisions with exchange rate ex_v2 = S_qwen_v2 / 0.6731 = 1.0303, S_qwen_v2 = 0.6935 the round-3 v2-anchor from the inherited Qwen track-S fit recomputed by the round-3 fit driver): elicit_band_v2 = 0.0207; practical_scale_v2 = 0.0518; health_gate_v2 = 0.0515. G0v2 gate (Qwen anchor + Gram-vs-primal parity) PASS at abs_dev 5.9e-6 vs committed 0.6731 and 2.2e-16 primal-vs-Gram agreement at n_train=4000, d=3584. G1v2 gate (RLVR × LMSYS23k chat vs 0.20606 bar) PASS at raw R² 0.6201 / recal 0.6200. Capture-parity gate (100 rows × 32 layers) PASS at min mean cosine 1.0000005 vs 0.999 threshold. All three gates were plan-registered in plan v13; no descope fired. No LLM judge is involved: the DV is an activation-geometry read.

# The Llama Tülu ladder's DPO→RLVR step needs at most a rotation of the linear context→answer map on seven of eight corpora, and no coordinate change on four of eight (raw) / six of eight (recal companion) (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

**Methodology:** [docs/methodology/issue_1336.md](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/blob/2249cf495d8c2d355b2f37f7b84eb7bf396f005d/docs/methodology/issue_1336.md) · [gist mirror](https://gist.github.com/superkaiba/5575c7b1da67014bf781a56e30ca6b88) *(rounds 1–2; the round-3 metric-ladder recipe is added inline under Methodology below and will be re-exported on promotion.)*

## Takeaways

- **The two DPO→RLVR corpora that need a coordinate change are the two RLVR trained on.** MATH closes at a rotation (tier 5, Δ_tier8 +0.008); IF-constraints escapes the 0.021 band at Δ_tier8 +0.025. The other six corpora close inside the band (four at tier 0 raw, six at tier 0 on the recal companion). RLVR adds a small, bounded, corpus-specific move on its own training distribution and no detectable cross-corpus move.
- **SFT installs the linear map; the base never reconstructs any post-trained map.** All 32 base→⟨SFT, DPO, RLVR, longer-RLVR⟩ × 8-corpora cells have Δ_tier8 between +0.14 and +0.26 (max +0.263 at base→longer-RLVR × MATH), orders of magnitude above the 0.021 band.
- **RLVR is closer to DPO than DPO is to SFT.** DPO→RLVR closes at tier ≤ 5 on 7/8 corpora raw; SFT→DPO closes at tier ≤ 5 on only 1/8, climbs to tier 7 or 8 on 5/8, and "none" on 2/8. On GSM8K test / train the SFT→DPO gap is small in R² but high-order — needs a full linear reparameterization at tier 8.
- **Longer-RLVR (Tülu-3.1) accumulates more coordinate change than the single-RLVR step, not less.** DPO→longer moves 4/8 corpora to a higher sufficient tier (IF Δ +0.025 → +0.116, UF t0 → "none", GSM8K test t2 → t8, GSM8K train t3 → t8). The map moves monotonically with RLVR dose.
- **Scope + alternative reading.** One released ladder, one fold seed 0, one corpus seed 1336; CIs are within-run bootstraps, not seed replication — confidence MODERATE. The small DPO→RLVR shift is also consistent with RLVR training touching fewer weights than SFT; a single ladder cannot separate that from "no new linear coordinates".

## Goal

- **This experiment in context:** [#825](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/825) found on Qwen2.5-7B that post-training does not create the linear context→answer map: the pretrained model carries it at 87% of instruct strength, and the instruct map is reconstructible from the base map by a general linear change of coordinates to within 0.0003 R² (map construct from [#779](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/779)). Qwen2.5 predates RLVR, so #825 tested only SFT/DPO-era post-training. Round 1 extended the read to the only released RLVR-bearing ladder (Llama-3.1-8B Tülu-3) at 5,000 prompts. Round 3 (this round) scales the corpus scope 3.8× on GSM8K, 3× on LMSYS, and adds four stage-matched corpora (MATH, IF-constraints, UltraFeedback, Tülu-3 SFT-mix), and replaces the single reparameterization gap with a 9-tier metric ladder (direct transfer → offsets → scaling → rotation → linear reparameterization of contexts / answers / both) — so "elicitation" resolves into which correction class suffices per stage-pair × corpus. Round 3 diverges from [#825](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/825) in that the base map here does NOT reconstruct any post-trained map at t ≤ 8 (Δ_tier8 +0.14 to +0.26); a cross-model divergence (Llama-3.1 vs Qwen-2.5), not a contradiction of the elicitation reading, and a second RLVR checkpoint tests dose.
- **Broader narrative:** This serves the contextual-vs-base identity question (`docs/open_questions.md`, identity-contextual-vs-base anchor): does post-training teach new context→answer structure, or re-expose structure the pretrained model already has? RLVR on verifiable rewards is the strongest published candidate for genuine teaching, so a tight null across the DPO→RLVR pair — plus the tier-ladder resolution that SFT→DPO needs a strictly higher tier than DPO→RLVR on 5/8 corpora, and that the two DPO→RLVR non-null corpora are exactly the RLVR training-mix distributions — is the most informative single read for the elicitation-not-teaching account. Two caveats bound it. First, DPO→longer-RLVR shows the map DOES move with further RLVR training on 4/8 corpora, so "RLVR doesn't change the map" is really "the single Tülu-3 RLVR step doesn't move the map beyond a rotation on the corpora it wasn't trained on". Second, a single ladder cannot separate "RLVR doesn't teach new coordinates" from "RLVR training on this ladder used a smaller effective weight update than the SFT step" — plausible because RLVR literature suggests low-rank effective updates; separating them would need a second ladder or a paired weight-space read.

## Methodology

**Design:** Five released checkpoints of one ladder — `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B` (base), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-DPO`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B` (post-RLVR), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3.1-8B` (longer-RLVR) — crossed in round 3 with eight prompt corpora and one render format per corpus, giving 40 generation cells and 56 stage-pair × corpus × layer-30 metric-ladder pair files (7 stage-pairs × 8 corpora). The post-training stage is the single manipulated variable; corpora, renders, sampling, and the fit recipe are held fixed. Round 3 corpora (revision-pinned): `chat` render on GSM8K test (1,319), GSM8K train full (7,473), MATH (7,500 from the RLVR mix), IF-constraints (11,000 sampled from the RLVR mix's ifeval component), UltraFeedback prompts (11,000 from the Tülu-3 8B preference mixture), Tülu-3 SFT-mix (11,000, stratified 3,667/3,667/3,666 across wildchat/flan/evol-codealpaca; corpus slug `sft11k`), and LMSYS-Chat-1M (23,000 sampled to yield ~15,000 kept); `naturalistic` render on LMSYS only. Rounds 1–2 (5,000 LMSYS × 2 renders + 5,000 GSM8K train + 1,319 GSM8K test) are superseded by the fatter round-3 corpora except the GSM8K test cell, which is retained as the decontaminated companion under the `n<d` caveat below. Per the standing both-mappings rule, the context-based mapping ran on every corpus × format; the prefix-based mapping (`xprefix`) ran on `naturalistic_lmsys23k` only — the chat-template prefix slot is row-constant by construction (measured max pairwise cosine distance up to 1.5e-4), so its map is degenerate at every stage. The naturalistic prefix mapping ran and reads R² 0.001–0.005 across all five stages (base 0.005; SFT/DPO/RLVR/longer-RLVR all 0.001) — floor-limited, invariant across stages, carried as an uncovered signal cell (a scope caveat, not a null).

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** Round 3 spent 194.37 GPU-h against a budgeted 98 GPU-h (2.0× over budget; deviation from plan §11, recorded here; the fit + metric-ladder phase's per-cell wall was under-estimated at plan time — the pilot batteries measured 541s/corpus vs the planned 1.4 h/corpus, but the mass of stage-corpus cells at 15–17k rows in generation + capture drove the wall).

**Evaluation:** Per (stage-pair p, corpus s, layer L=30) the reparameterization ladder produces held-out R² of the source map applied to target contexts at every tier t ∈ {0..8}, on the same rows and folds as the target's within-stage map. Tiers, per `docs/mapping_similarity_metrics.md`: t0 direct transfer (ŷ = W_s x + b_s applied unchanged), t1 context offset (ŷ = W_s (x − Δx) + b_s, Δx from cloud means only), t2 answer offset (Δy on the output side), t3 bias offset (refit b* only), t4 global scaling (α W_s x + b*), t5 mapping rotation (R W_s x + b*, orthogonal Procrustes on directions), t6 linear reparameterization of contexts, t7 linear reparameterization of answers, t8 both (A ∘ W_s ∘ B). All offsets fit on clouds alone (never on paired context→answer rows). Δ_t = within-stage R² − tier-t R². The sufficient-tier statistic is min{t ∈ 0..8 : Δ_t ≤ 0.021 · ex_v2 = 0.0207} at the paired prompt-level bootstrap point estimate; "none ≤ 8" is a reportable value. Primary scale is raw pooled R² (round 3's fatter fold-train regime makes the recalibration rescue used in rounds 1–2 unnecessary — G0v2/G1v2 both PASS at raw); the held-out cross-fitted per-dim affine recalibration companion is always computed. The recalibration companion adds 4,096 per-dim scalar shift+scale parameters cross-fitted from folds, so a genuine map-mismatch signal can be partially absorbed by it; recal disagrees with raw on 3/8 corpora for DPO→RLVR (GSM8K test raw t2 → recal t0; GSM8K train raw t3 → recal t0; IF-constraints raw "none" → recal t8), so raw is the binding read and recal is reported as the companion that a per-dim rescaling accommodates. The stage-of-record contrast C_v2 = Δ_tier8(RLVR, gsm8k_train_full, chat) − Δ_tier8(DPO, gsm8k_train_full, chat) on the RLVR training distribution: point −0.0031 with a bootstrap 95% CI running from −0.0039 to −0.0024 on the raw scale (a signed negative CI — reparameterized-DPO reconstructs RLVR marginally better than reparameterized-base reconstructs DPO on that corpus; magnitude 5× smaller than the 0.021 elicit band, sign is direction-of-effect, not "matches to zero"). Registered decision constants (round-3 revisions with ex_v2 = S_qwen_v2 / 0.6731 = 1.0303, S_qwen_v2 = 0.6935): elicit_band_v2 = 0.0207; practical_scale_v2 = 0.0518; health_gate_v2 = 0.0515. G0v2 (Qwen anchor + Gram-vs-primal parity) PASS at abs_dev 5.9e-6 and 2.2e-16 primal-vs-Gram agreement. G1v2 (RLVR × LMSYS23k chat vs 0.20606 bar) PASS at raw R² 0.6201 / recal 0.6200. Capture-parity gate (100 rows × 32 layers) PASS at min mean cosine 1.0000005 vs 0.999 threshold. All three gates were plan-registered in plan v13; no descope fired. No LLM judge is involved: the DV is an activation-geometry read.

### The base map never reconstructs a post-trained map; the SFT step installs the map, and every later step is a coordinate change

Mean across 8 corpora of the source-map R² at each of the 9 tiers, layer 30, raw pooled R². The four base→⟨stage⟩ pairs start at t0 R² between −0.52 (base→SFT mean) and −1.59 (base→RLVR mean); per-corpus t0 floor is −4.56 (base→RLVR × MATH). ### The fitted maps are strongly discriminative: identity+bias fails at R² ≈ −3, kNN acc@1 reaches 0.5 to 0.8

Within-stage identity+bias baseline (ŷ = x + b, b = train-fold mean of y − x) per the standing "identity+bias baseline AND kNN-retrieval metric" rule: deeply negative across every stage × corpus cell — R² from −0.95 (base→SFT × MATH) to −4.56 (base→RLVR × MATH), mean around −2.7. "Predict answer = context + shift" is far worse than the mean baseline everywhere. kNN retrieval on the fitted within-stage maps hits acc@1 0.48–0.73 (euclidean) / 0.54–0.76 (cosine) at k=1 over the 2,000-row held-out pool, chance = 1/2000 = 0.0005 — three orders of magnitude above chance. Representative cell (DPO→RLVR × GSM8K train): within R² 0.480, identity+bias R² −3.36, kNN acc@1 (euclidean) 0.726, acc@5 0.867, median rank 1.0, MRR 0.79. # The Llama Tülu ladder's DPO→RLVR step needs at most a rotation of the linear context→answer map on seven of eight corpora, and no coordinate change on four of eight (raw) / six of eight (recal companion) (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

**Methodology:** [docs/methodology/issue_1336.md](https://github.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/blob/2249cf495d8c2d355b2f37f7b84eb7bf396f005d/docs/methodology/issue_1336.md) · [gist mirror](https://gist.github.com/superkaiba/5575c7b1da67014bf781a56e30ca6b88) *(rounds 1–2; the round-3 metric-ladder recipe is added inline under Methodology below and will be re-exported on promotion.)*

## Takeaways

- **The two DPO→RLVR corpora that need a coordinate change are the two RLVR trained on.** MATH closes at a rotation (tier 5, Δ_tier8 +0.008); IF-constraints escapes the 0.021 band at Δ_tier8 +0.025. The other six corpora close inside the band (four at tier 0 raw, six at tier 0 on the recal companion). RLVR adds a small, bounded, corpus-specific move on its own training distribution and no detectable cross-corpus move.
- **SFT installs the linear map; the base never reconstructs any post-trained map.** All 32 base→⟨SFT, DPO, RLVR, longer-RLVR⟩ × 8-corpora cells have Δ_tier8 between +0.14 and +0.26 (max +0.263 at base→longer-RLVR × MATH), orders of magnitude above the 0.021 band.
- **RLVR is closer to DPO than DPO is to SFT.** DPO→RLVR closes at tier ≤ 5 on 7/8 corpora raw; SFT→DPO closes at tier ≤ 5 on only 1/8, climbs to tier 7 or 8 on 5/8, and "none" on 2/8. On GSM8K test / train the SFT→DPO gap is small in R² but high-order — needs a full linear reparameterization at tier 8.
- **Longer-RLVR (Tülu-3.1) accumulates more coordinate change than the single-RLVR step, not less.** DPO→longer moves 4/8 corpora to a higher sufficient tier (IF Δ +0.025 → +0.116, UF t0 → "none", GSM8K test t2 → t8, GSM8K train t3 → t8). The map moves monotonically with RLVR dose.
- **Scope + alternative reading.** One released ladder, one fold seed 0, one corpus seed 1336; CIs are within-run bootstraps, not seed replication — confidence MODERATE. The small DPO→RLVR shift is also consistent with RLVR training touching fewer weights than SFT; a single ladder cannot separate that from "no new linear coordinates".

## Goal

- **This experiment in context:** [#825](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/825) found on Qwen2.5-7B that post-training does not create the linear context→answer map: the pretrained model carries it at 87% of instruct strength, and the instruct map is reconstructible from the base map by a general linear change of coordinates to within 0.0003 R² (map construct from [#779](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/779)). Qwen2.5 predates RLVR, so #825 tested only SFT/DPO-era post-training. Round 1 extended the read to the only released RLVR-bearing ladder (Llama-3.1-8B Tülu-3) at 5,000 prompts. Round 3 (this round) scales the corpus scope 3.8× on GSM8K, 3× on LMSYS, and adds four stage-matched corpora (MATH, IF-constraints, UltraFeedback, Tülu-3 SFT-mix), and replaces the single reparameterization gap with a 9-tier metric ladder (direct transfer → offsets → scaling → rotation → linear reparameterization of contexts / answers / both) — so "elicitation" resolves into which correction class suffices per stage-pair × corpus. Round 3 diverges from [#825](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/825) in that the base map here does NOT reconstruct any post-trained map at t ≤ 8 (Δ_tier8 +0.14 to +0.26); a cross-model divergence (Llama-3.1 vs Qwen-2.5), not a contradiction of the elicitation reading, and a second RLVR checkpoint tests dose.
- **Broader narrative:** This serves the contextual-vs-base identity question (`docs/open_questions.md`, identity-contextual-vs-base anchor): does post-training teach new context→answer structure, or re-expose structure the pretrained model already has? RLVR on verifiable rewards is the strongest published candidate for genuine teaching, so a tight null across the DPO→RLVR pair — plus the tier-ladder resolution that SFT→DPO needs a strictly higher tier than DPO→RLVR on 5/8 corpora, and that the two DPO→RLVR non-null corpora are exactly the RLVR training-mix distributions — is the most informative single read for the elicitation-not-teaching account. Two caveats bound it. First, DPO→longer-RLVR shows the map DOES move with further RLVR training on 4/8 corpora, so "RLVR doesn't change the map" is really "the single Tülu-3 RLVR step doesn't move the map beyond a rotation on the corpora it wasn't trained on". Second, a single ladder cannot separate "RLVR doesn't teach new coordinates" from "RLVR training on this ladder used a smaller effective weight update than the SFT step" — plausible because RLVR literature suggests low-rank effective updates; separating them would need a second ladder or a paired weight-space read.

## Methodology

**Design:** Five released checkpoints of one ladder — `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B` (base), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-DPO`, `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B` (post-RLVR), `allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3.1-8B` (longer-RLVR) — crossed in round 3 with eight prompt corpora and one render format per corpus, giving 40 generation cells and 56 stage-pair × corpus × layer-30 metric-ladder pair files (7 stage-pairs × 8 corpora). The post-training stage is the single manipulated variable; corpora, renders, sampling, and the fit recipe are held fixed. Round 3 corpora (revision-pinned): `chat` render on GSM8K test (1,319), GSM8K train full (7,473), MATH (7,500 from the RLVR mix), IF-constraints (11,000 sampled from the RLVR mix's ifeval component), UltraFeedback prompts (11,000 from the Tülu-3 8B preference mixture), Tülu-3 SFT-mix (11,000, stratified 3,667/3,667/3,666 across wildchat/flan/evol-codealpaca; corpus slug `sft11k`), and LMSYS-Chat-1M (23,000 sampled to yield ~15,000 kept); `naturalistic` render on LMSYS only. Rounds 1–2 (5,000 LMSYS × 2 renders + 5,000 GSM8K train + 1,319 GSM8K test) are superseded by the fatter round-3 corpora except the GSM8K test cell, which is retained as the decontaminated companion under the `n<d` caveat below. Per the standing both-mappings rule, the context-based mapping ran on every corpus × format; the prefix-based mapping (`xprefix`) ran on `naturalistic_lmsys23k` only — the chat-template prefix slot is row-constant by construction (measured max pairwise cosine distance up to 1.5e-4), so its map is degenerate at every stage. The naturalistic prefix mapping ran and reads R² 0.001–0.005 across all five stages (base 0.005; SFT/DPO/RLVR/longer-RLVR all 0.001) — floor-limited, invariant across stages, carried as an uncovered signal cell (a scope caveat, not a null).

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** Round 3 spent 194.37 GPU-h against a budgeted 98 GPU-h (2.0× over budget; deviation from plan §11, recorded here; the fit + metric-ladder phase's per-cell wall was under-estimated at plan time — the pilot batteries measured 541s/corpus vs the planned 1.4 h/corpus, but the mass of stage-corpus cells at 15–17k rows in generation + capture drove the wall).

**Evaluation:** Per (stage-pair p, corpus s, layer L=30) the reparameterization ladder produces held-out R² of the source map applied to target contexts at every tier t ∈ {0..8}, on the same rows and folds as the target's within-stage map. Tiers, per `docs/mapping_similarity_metrics.md`: t0 direct transfer (ŷ = W_s x + b_s applied unchanged), t1 context offset (ŷ = W_s (x − Δx) + b_s, Δx from cloud means only), t2 answer offset (Δy on the output side), t3 bias offset (refit b* only), t4 global scaling (α W_s x + b*), t5 mapping rotation (R W_s x + b*, orthogonal Procrustes on directions), t6 linear reparameterization of contexts, t7 linear reparameterization of answers, t8 both (A ∘ W_s ∘ B). All offsets fit on clouds alone (never on paired context→answer rows). Δ_t = within-stage R² − tier-t R². The sufficient-tier statistic is min{t ∈ 0..8 : Δ_t ≤ 0.021 · ex_v2 = 0.0207} at the paired prompt-level bootstrap point estimate; "none ≤ 8" is a reportable value. Primary scale is raw pooled R² (round 3's fatter fold-train regime makes the recalibration rescue used in rounds 1–2 unnecessary — G0v2/G1v2 both PASS at raw); the held-out cross-fitted per-dim affine recalibration companion is always computed. The recalibration companion adds 4,096 per-dim scalar shift+scale parameters cross-fitted from folds, so a genuine map-mismatch signal can be partially absorbed by it; recal disagrees with raw on 3/8 corpora for DPO→RLVR (GSM8K test raw t2 → recal t0; GSM8K train raw t3 → recal t0; IF-constraints raw "none" → recal t8), so raw is the binding read and recal is reported as the companion that a per-dim rescaling accommodates. The stage-of-record contrast C_v2 = Δ_tier8(dpo→rlvr, gsm8k_train_full, chat) on the RLVR training distribution: point −0.0031 with a bootstrap 95% CI running from −0.0039 to −0.0024 on the raw scale (a signed negative CI — reparameterized-DPO reconstructs RLVR marginally better than the within-RLVR fit on that corpus; magnitude 5× smaller than the 0.021 elicit band, sign is direction-of-effect, not "matches to zero"). Registered decision constants (round-3 revisions with ex_v2 = S_qwen_v2 / 0.6731 = 1.0303, S_qwen_v2 = 0.6935): elicit_band_v2 = 0.0207; practical_scale_v2 = 0.0518; health_gate_v2 = 0.0515. G0v2 (Qwen anchor + Gram-vs-primal parity) PASS at abs_dev 5.9e-6 and 2.2e-16 primal-vs-Gram agreement. G1v2 (RLVR × LMSYS23k chat vs 0.20606 bar) PASS at raw R² 0.6201 / recal 0.6200. Capture-parity gate (100 rows × 32 layers) PASS at min mean cosine 1.0000005 vs 0.999 threshold. All three gates were plan-registered in plan v13; no descope fired. No LLM judge is involved: the DV is an activation-geometry read.

Each cell is the cheapest correction — tier 0 (source map unchanged) to 8 (linear reparameterization of both sides) — whose gap Δ_t = within-stage R² − tier-t R² falls inside a 0.021-wide window around zero at the paired-bootstrap point estimate; "×" means no tier ≤ 8 suffices. Δ = tier-8 gap point estimate.

### The base map never reconstructs a post-trained map; the SFT step installs the map, and every later step is a coordinate change

Mean across 8 corpora of the source-map R² at each of the 9 tiers, layer 30, raw pooled R². The four base→⟨stage⟩ pairs start at t0 R² between −0.52 (base→SFT mean) and −1.59 (base→RLVR mean); per-corpus t0 floor is −4.56 (base→RLVR × MATH). They climb to R² 0.33–0.36 at t8, still well below the within-stage ceiling ≈ 0.55.

![Tier-by-tier R² recovery ladder per stage-pair, mean across 8 corpora with across-corpus 1 sigma bands, layer 30, raw pooled R²](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/b9ef76654c66a7f18e1f04ece3c4908d406e4960/figures/issue_1336/metric_ladder_tier_profile.png)

> **Figure.** *Stage-pair R² recovery curves separate cleanly.* Mean R² across 8 corpora per tier (t0 direct → t8 full linear reparam), layer 30, raw; bands ±1σ across corpora. base→⟨stage⟩ pairs rise from R² between −0.5 (base→SFT) and −1.6 (base→RLVR) at t0 to R² 0.34–0.36 at t8. DPO→RLVR and DPO→longer-RLVR sit above R² 0.42 at every tier and are nearly flat. SFT→DPO starts at R² 0.27 at t0, dips below zero on 2/8 corpora (GSM8K test, MATH), and climbs to ≥ 0.55 by t5.

The three post-training pairs start at very different t0 means — SFT→DPO 0.27 (2/8 corpora below zero: GSM8K test −0.09, MATH −0.18), DPO→RLVR 0.51 (all 8 positive), DPO→longer 0.43 (all 8 positive). No linear reparameterization of the base map reconstructs any post-trained map at t ≤ 8; a small linear correction of the DPO map often suffices for RLVR. Post-training installs the map at SFT; the Tülu-3 RLVR step moves the coordinate system less than DPO did on 7/8 corpora.

### The fitted maps are strongly discriminative: identity+bias fails at R² ≈ −3, kNN acc@1 reaches 0.38 to 0.86

Within-stage identity+bias baseline (ŷ = x + b, b = train-fold mean of y − x) per the standing baseline+kNN rule is deeply negative on every stage × corpus cell — R² from −0.95 (base→SFT × MATH) to −3.41 (base→DPO × sft11k), mean −2.7. "Predict answer = context + shift" is far worse than the mean baseline everywhere. kNN retrieval on the fitted within-stage maps hits acc@1 0.38–0.85 (euclidean) / 0.39–0.86 (cosine) across the 56 cells (held-out pool 2,000 for 7/8 corpora, 1,319 for GSM8K test), chance ≤ 0.001 — three orders of magnitude above chance. The DPO→RLVR row: euclidean 0.38–0.73, cosine 0.39–0.76 across its 8 corpora. Representative cell (DPO→RLVR × GSM8K train): within R² 0.480, identity+bias −3.36, kNN acc@1 0.726, MRR 0.79. Per-cell values at `per_layer.30.baselines.within` in every pair file at [eval_results_mirror_v2/metric_ladder/ @ 34333a0bde](https://huggingface.co/datasets/superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-data/tree/34333a0bde8d1e8401b69520074195c2ca4f6f26/issue1336_rlvr_ladder/eval_results_mirror_v2/metric_ladder). "DPO→RLVR needs no coordinate change on 4/8 corpora" describes agreement between two strongly discriminative maps, not two vacuous ones.

  composition + kernel reduction order. The regen deliberately runs a DIFFERENT engine
  (max_model_len 5120 vs the original's) on a DIFFERENT batch (5 rows vs 1319), so the RNG

ROUND A — PREFIX-CONTINUATION REGEN (replaces the falsified resample mechanism)
=====================================================================
MECHANISM CHANGE (this is the whole point). The pilot proved re-sampling from the original
prompt is a fresh draw, not a continuation (prefix_match 0/5; regenerated answers came back
mean 885 tokens against a >=1024 truncation). The replacement PREFILLS the stored truncated
answer as part of the prompt and generates only the TAIL, so the stored prefix is byte-identical
BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck. P(tail | prompt, stored prefix) is exactly the conditional
the uncapped run would have sampled from, so there is no selection-on-outcome resample bias.

  current  texts = [prompt_builder(r["prompt"]) for r in trunc]          -> re-samples
  new      texts = [prompt_builder(r["prompt"]) + r["response"] ...]     -> continues

CAP ARITHMETIC (the load-bearing detail). A row with finish_reason == "length" hit the ORIGINAL
cap exactly, so every stored truncated answer is exactly 1024 tokens. A uniform TAIL cap of 1024
therefore gives a total answer budget of exactly 2048 — identical semantics to a whole-cell
2048-cap regen for these rows, with no per-row SamplingParams needed. The engine's existing
--max-model-len 5120 already fits it exactly: 3072 prompt budget + 1024 stored + 1024 tail.
The script's current assert (max_model_len - max_tokens == cm.PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET) must be
re-derived for continuation mode, where the effective prompt now carries the stored answer:
  max_model_len - tail_cap == cm.PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET + original_cap   (5120 - 1024 == 3072 + 1024)
Keeping the OLD assert unchanged would refuse the correct invocation; weakening it to nothing
would let a wrong cap through silently. It gets re-derived, not deleted.

DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCES the implementer must carry: the generated `raw` is now the TAIL only, so
the persisted answer is stored+raw; new_answer_tokens counts the FULL answer; prefix_match
becomes an ASSERT (True by construction — a False is a bug, not a statistic) and the audit keeps
prefix_common_frac as the residual diagnostic; the >=2048-token render-budget validation now
sees longer conversations, so the existing DROP path for over-budget renders will fire more often
and its rate must be reported.

exposes `--cells <comma list of source__target__format__corpus>` and a separate `--stage` flag,
and `stage_inputs` stages only what the passed cells need (with an "already staged" skip).

  (sft,rlvr_long), (rlvr,rlvr_long) at that surface — needing exactly 4 turnstore dirs
  (one per model at that surface), i.e. ~33.6 GB.
  Loop: stage those 4 -> fit those 4 cells -> REAP the staged dirs -> next surface.
  PEAK local footprint ~34 GB instead of 268 GB; total download still 268 GB (unavoidable — the
  fits must read every turnstore once), which is bandwidth, not disk.
  This is the same between-phase incremental-reap discipline the disk-hygiene rule mandates, and
  the reap is safe by the rule's own test: the reaped dirs are STAGED, re-downloadable copies

  outputs are written (the fits are the last consumer of that surface's turnstores — nothing
  later reads them, which is the #1489 last-consumer condition).

=== BLOCKER 1 (surfaced by the implementing subagent): does the render budget censor the very rows
    the regen exists to recover?

The subagent reported that rows whose tail runs long exceed MAX_CONV_TOKENS=2048 (the WHOLE rendered
conversation budget, src/explore_persona_space/experiments/issue_825/common.py:31) and drop as
`over_token_budget` in scripts/issue1336_render.py::validate_render. The concern was that this
re-censors exactly the long-answer rows the truncation regen targets — inverting the original
truncation bias rather than removing it.

DETERMINATION: the constraint is GENUINE, not an inherited default. The same 2048-token check is
enforced at GENERATION time (issue825_gen_conversations.py:447) AND at turnstore EXTRACTION
(issue1336_extract_turnstore.py imports validate_render), so a conversation over budget cannot enter
a turnstore by any path. Raising MAX_CONV_TOKENS is off the table: it would break comparability with
every banked #825/#1336 turnstore.

But the censoring is FAR milder than feared. Measured headroom = MAX_CONV_TOKENS - len(rendered
conversation with the STORED truncated answer), i.e. the tail tokens a continuation may add before
the row drops (probe: 2 local cells, both formats, cached tokenizers):

  cell             truncated  median headroom  >=512 tok  >=1024 tok
  rlvr/lmsys5k     260/5000   981              96.2%      0%
  dpo/lmsys5k      245/5000   981              97.1%      0%

LMSYS first turns are short (prompt+template ~43 tokens median), so a truncated row has ~981 tokens
of room — the effective answer budget is ~2x the original 1024 cap. The drop bites only rows whose
true answer needs >~1000 MORE tokens, and those are unusable downstream regardless (the extractor
applies the same check). 9-12 of the truncated rows per cell are ALREADY over budget with the stored
answer alone (min headroom -150) and were dropped at gen time; they will drop again, as expected.

DESIGN CONFIRMED AS-IS: the uniform 1024-token tail cap is correct. Clamping the tail cap to each
row's headroom would produce a still-truncated tail that PASSES the budget check — silently
re-introducing the truncation bias the round exists to remove. Dropping is the honest outcome: a row
that goes over budget is either still-truncated or complete-but-unrepresentable, both unusable.
The raw stored+tail text is persisted in answers.jsonl with kept=False, so nothing is lost.

=== BLOCKER 2 (found by pre-flight probe; would have killed the production run on cell 1)

`assert_stored_answers_at_cap` required every stored truncated answer to re-tokenize to EXACTLY
cm.SAMPLING["max_tokens"] (1024). Measured against real rows:

  rlvr/lmsys5k  228/260 exact  (32 rows off, 12.3%)   deltas: -6,-4,-3,-2,-1,+1,+2
  dpo/lmsys5k   224/245 exact  (21 rows off,  8.6%)   deltas: -4,-2,-1,+1,+2

All deltas are tiny and two-sided: this is detokenize->retokenize BPE seam drift on the STORED TEXT,
not role-header truncation (which would show large NEGATIVE deltas). The assert is per-row and
fail-loud, so the first drifted row would have aborted the whole cell.

FIX: STORED_CAP_TOKEN_TOLERANCE = 16 — an order of magnitude above the measured -6..+2 drift, far
below any real role-header cut (a cut at a role marker in a cap-truncated answer removes
tens-to-hundreds of tokens), so the band separates the two causes cleanly. Within the band the row
IS an at-cap row and the residual shifts the realized total budget by a few tokens out of ~2048
(immaterial); outside it the assert still fails loud naming the row and its delta. The function now
RETURNS the realized drift distribution, recorded in the audit as `stored_cap_token_drift`, so a
band drifting toward saturation is visible rather than silent. Tests updated: the exact-equality pin
became a drift-tolerance pin (both directions, plus one-token-past-the-band still refusing);
9 passed.

=== WHAT HAPPENED

Invocation 1 (base/chat, cheapest-... no: highest-truncation-first, lmsys23k) loaded the engine in
199.8s and aborted on the very first cell:

  AssertionError: stored answer for prompt_idx=5020 re-tokenizes to 89 tokens, off original cap
  1024 by -935 (> tolerance 16) — row did not come from the cap

Driver stopped with rc=1, cells_on_disk=0 — no partial or wrongly-budgeted output was written. The
fail-loud band did exactly its job: 89 tokens is not BPE round-trip drift (measured -6..+2), so a
uniform 1024-token tail budget would have been WRONG for that row, and it refused rather than
silently continue. This is the edge case the pilot round named in its option-1 note ("one edge case
to check — rows where _truncate_role_headers shortened a length-finish row's stored text"). It is
not rare.

=== MEASURED: 25.4% OF LENGTH-FINISH ROWS ARE NOT CONTINUABLE

Probed the production basis cell directly (base/lmsys23k, 18,000 source rows, tokenizer
meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, counts only — no corpus text read into context):

  finish_reason == "length"            3,220
    stored ~at cap (continuable)       2,401   (kept 1,916 / dropped 485)
    stored far short (role-stripped)     818   (kept   652 / dropped 166)   = 25.4%
    stored above band                      1   (kept     1)
  role-stripped stored token counts: min 0, p25 22, median 61, p75 210, max 1,006

=== WHY finish_reason == "length" DOES NOT IMPLY "cut by the cap"

The engine stops at 1024 TOKENS, but what gets PERSISTED is the answer after
_truncate_role_headers removes a hallucinated next turn. So a row can hit the cap while its stored
ANSWER ended much earlier: the model answered in ~61 tokens, started a fake new turn, and the strip
removed everything from the role marker on.

For those rows a continuation is not just ill-budgeted, it is WRONG IN KIND. The decisive argument:
an UNCAPPED run would have generated more text past 1024 tokens, but all of it sits AFTER the role
marker, so the strip would have removed it too — leaving byte-identical stored text. These rows are
therefore NOT length-censored at all. Appending a continuation would fabricate text after an answer
that already terminated, which is a worse artifact than the censoring the round exists to remove.

=== DESIGN DECISION: PARTITION, NOT ABORT (and not continue)

assert_stored_answers_at_cap is replaced by partition_truncated_by_stored_length, a three-way split:

  stored >= cap - 16                     CONTINUABLE  -> regenerate the tail (unchanged mechanism)
  stored <  cap - 16                     ROLE-HEADER-STRIPPED -> SKIP, count, report
  stored >  1.5x cap                     FAIL LOUD    -> no drift or strip can produce this; the
                                                        pool, cap, or tokenizer is not what the
                                                        script assumes

The upper fail-loud bound moved from cap+16 to 1.5x cap deliberately: the single above-band row is
plausible drift on a different corpus, and continuing from a slightly-long prefix is harmless (the
render budget check drops it honestly if the total overruns). Reserving the hard error for a
genuinely impossible length keeps the loud signal meaningful.

Every cell's audit.json now carries `stored_length_partition` (counts, the stripped rows' length
distribution, and the drift distribution of the CONTINUABLE rows only) plus
`n_role_header_stripped_skipped` and `n_source_length_finish`. The skip count is the regen's honest
denominator, not a failure.

=== POPULATION CONSEQUENCE (third sizing revision)

The 46,289 figure in v188 counted KEPT length-finish rows. If base/lmsys23k's 25.4% strip fraction
is representative, the genuinely continuable population is roughly three quarters of that — order

## Fold-count floor guard (brief check 3 — the round's biggest risk)

`n_folds_eff = max(2, min(POOLED_N_FOLDS, len(train_keys) // 2))` in `_assign_given_labels`, WARNING-logged when ≠ 5, recorded as manifest `n_folds`; consumers (`run_pooled_v3` → `pooled_folds = int(man.get("n_folds", args.folds))` with a printed notice; `run_g0v3` likewise) follow the manifest, and `run_pooled_cell`'s pre-existing assert (`fit_cells.py:1500-1502` `len(uniq_folds) == n_folds`) stays fail-loud on manifest-internal inconsistency.

Demonstrated bound (from the code, not asserted):
- Guaranteed by construction: per-corpus test rows ≤ 0.28·n_c < n_c, so EVERY corpus keeps ≥ 1 train group ⇒ train groups ≥ 7 ⇒ `n_folds_eff ≥ 3` with ≥ 2 groups (≥ 2 rows) per fold. So a strict "5 always" is NOT guaranteed by construction alone.
- `n_folds_eff = 5` requires train groups ≥ 10 of the ~166 (plan-realized k_c 45/24/24/22/22/19/10). For the guard to bind, ≥ 157 of 166 groups must land test/merged while test rows stay ≤ 28% per corpus — i.e. essentially every corpus's k-means must produce one ≥ 72%-mass cluster plus fragments (lmsys: one 9,693-row cluster at k=45 against a ~300-row target), simultaneously in all 7 corpora. At the plan's realized shape train groups ≈ 130+, so the guard is production-inert for any non-degenerate clustering.
- Residual regime is NOT silent: WARNING log + manifest `n_folds` + the fit-side "pooled folds follow the manifest: N (--folds=5 ignored...)" notice. The brief's blocker criterion (silently ship n_folds≠5 without halting or recording) is therefore not met — it records. I verified the trip/clear pair live: my own smoke re-run reproduced the guard (16 rows → 7 train groups → `fold count floor-guarded to 3`, manifest `n_folds: 3`, folds {0,1,2}, rc=0).

Minor (below) recommends closing the residual with a 2-line full-mode equality halt.

[stage-dispatch] Step 6 pre-launch finding — realized-width re-shard decision: 8 GPUs STANDS (wider is not reachable on this lane)

The dispatch steering note (v218) authorized one deviation without re-approval:
"RE-SHARD WIDER if the lane offers more than 8 GPUs at dispatch (realized-width
re-sharding is an allowed deviation without re-approval; 20 cell-atomic EXT_off
units collapse from 3 waves to 1 at >=20 GPUs)." I investigated whether that
authorization can be exercised. It cannot — on FOUR independent grounds, any one
of which is binding. Plan v17 §9's 8-GPU / 3-wave shape therefore stands
UNCHANGED, and this is a NON-deviation, not a silent narrowing.

**(1) The workload is single-node BY CONSTRUCTION.** `scripts/issue1336_dispatch.sh`
has ZERO multi-node awareness: a grep for `srun|SLURM_NNODES|SLURM_NODEID|SLURM_NODELIST|--nodes|MASTER_ADDR|torchrun`
returns 0 hits across the whole 4,000+-line dispatcher. It sizes its own width
from the LOCALLY visible GPU count —
`NGPU=$( (nvidia-smi --list-gpus 2>/dev/null || true) | wc -l )` (:91) — and
`run_queue()` (:135) fans out `width=$NGPU` (:139) workers, each pinned to one
local device via `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=w` (:173-174). A second allocated node
would sit completely idle: nothing in the dispatcher can address it.

**(2) The fellows nodes ARE 8-GPU.** Every charmander partition reports
`Gres=gpu:8` per node (general / overflow / dev alike). There is no wider node
to land on, so even a multi-node-capable workload could not get >8 GPUs on ONE
allocation unit.

**(3) The renderer would REFUSE a wider request.** `backends/slurm.py` carries
`max_gpus_per_node=8` for the fellows cluster config (:452) and asserts
`spec.gpus <= max_gpus_per_node` before submitting (:180-181). A `--gpus 16`
would fail at render time, not degrade gracefully.

**(4) The QoS caps per-user GPUs at 16 anyway.** `high-eur` (the first rung of
the #1899 ladder) sets `MaxTRESPU gres/gpu=16` (:463-466), as does `normal-eur`
— so the ceiling on this lane is 2 nodes' worth even for a workload that could
use them.

**Decision: dispatch at `--gpus 8` exactly as plan v17 §9 specifies.** Going
wider is not a re-shard — it would require writing multi-node coordination into
the dispatcher (an `srun`/`torchrun` launcher plus a cross-node work queue),
which is a code-change round well beyond "realized-width re-sharding," and the
steering note holds cell COUNT, corpora, `test_ratio`, DV, and the verdict
lattice as Must-ask. The 20 cell-atomic EXT_off units stay at 3 waves (8/8/4).

Worth recording: the dispatcher reads its width at RUNTIME from `nvidia-smi`,
so the collapse-to-1-wave behavior the steering note wanted is already wired for
free — it will fire automatically IF a wider single node ever hosts this
workload. Nothing needs changing for that to happen; this lane simply has no
such node.

**What halted.** `[pool] A4 HALT — packing window unsatisfiable after the single
registered k_c x2 retry for ['math7500']`. The A4 gate is correct and the halt is
sound — the run did NOT produce a bad split. But the halt is a SYMPTOM; the
registered `k_c × 2` retry is powerless against the real cause, by construction.

**Root cause — CONFIRMED by direct measurement, not inferred: mpnet truncation
collapses every math7500 embedding to one identical vector.**

- math7500's prompts are FEW-SHOT formatted: a fixed multi-exemplar preamble
  followed by the actual question at the END. Measured over a 400-prompt sample,
  the shared common prefix is **1,530 chars = 91.2% of the median prompt (1,678
  chars)**.
- That shared prefix alone tokenizes to **611 tokens**, while
  `sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2` has `max_seq_length = 384`. The
  encoder therefore never reaches ANY distinguishing content — it sees only
  boilerplate. (The tokenizer itself warns: `Token indices sequence length is
  longer than the specified maximum sequence length for this model (611 > 384)`.)
- Direct confirmation on 8 math7500 prompts: pairwise cosine
  **min = mean = max = 1.000000**, and **1 distinct embedding row out of 8**
  (byte-identical vectors).

So k-means on math7500 receives ~7,166 copies of ONE point and can only ever
return 1 distinct cluster (`[pool] math7500: n=7166 k_c=24 k_eff=1`, with
sklearn's `ConvergenceWarning: Number of distinct clusters (1) found smaller than
n_clusters (24). Possibly due to duplicate points in X`). Groups are atomic in a
cluster-aware split, so all 7,166 rows land in TRAIN ⇒ realized test share
**0/7166 = 0.0000**, outside the [0.15, 0.28] window. Doubling `k_c` 24 → 48
cannot separate identical points, so the registered retry re-collapsed to
`k_eff=1` and A4 halted. The prompts are individually DISTINCT (7,500/7,500
unique strings) — distinctness of the TEXT is not distinctness of the EMBEDDING,
which is precisely the trap here.

**This is the SAME defect that failed the run on 2026-08-07, surfacing through a
different gate — Option A relabeled it rather than retiring it.** The same
`c_pool.log` holds the earlier failure: `AssertionError: corpus-locked clusters
(fewer than 3 corpora)` whose composition line reads `cluster 2: n=7166
{'math7500': 7166}` — all of math7500 in ONE cluster even under v15's GLOBAL
k=50 k-means. Under v15 the degeneracy tripped `CLUSTER_MIN_CORPORA`; under v17's
per-corpus sub-clustering it trips the A4 packing window. Plan v17's premise that
per-corpus sub-clustering retires this failure class is therefore **falsified for
math7500**: it retires the ASSERT, not the pathology. This also SUPERSEDES the
`epm:progress v220` disposition that treated the v4 failure as
